title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe
authors: López-Otín C, Blasco MA, Partridge L, Serrano M, Kroemer G.
why: Updates the hallmarks framework to twelve interacting aging mechanisms.
caution: A framework for research, not a proven anti-aging treatment list.

title: In Vivo Amelioration of Age-Associated Hallmarks by Partial Reprogramming
authors: Ocampo A, Reddy P, Martinez-Redondo P, Platero-Luengo A, Hatanaka F, Hishida T, Li M, Lam D, Kurita M, Beyret E, Araoka T, Vazquez-Ferrer E, Donoso D, Roman JL, Xu J, Rodriguez Esteban C, Nuñez G, Nuñez Delicado E, Campistol JM, Guillen I, Guillen P, Izpisua Belmonte JC.
why: Cyclic partial reprogramming improves aging-related phenotypes and survival in progeroid mice.
caution: Premature-aging model survival does not establish normal human lifespan extension.

title: Reprogramming to recover youthful epigenetic information and restore vision
authors: Lu Y, Brommer B, Tian X, Krishnan A, Meer M, Wang C, Vera DL, Zeng Q, Yu D, Bonkowski MS, Yang JH, Zhou S, Hoffmann EM, Karg MM, Schultz MB, Kane AE, Davidsohn N, Korobkina E, Chwalek K, Rajman LA, Church GM, Church GM, Hochedlinger K, Gladyshev VN, Horvath S, Levine ME, Gregory-Ksander MS, Ksander BR, He Z, Sinclair DA.
why: OSK reprogramming restores regenerative and visual functions in mouse eyes.
caution: Tissue-specific mouse outcomes, not whole-person age reversal.

title: Cellular reprogramming and epigenetic rejuvenation
authors: Simpson DJ, Olova NN, Chandra T.
why: Explains how epigenetic rejuvenation might be separated from loss of cell identity.
caution: Translational strategy and review, not human efficacy evidence.

title: In vivo partial reprogramming alters age-associated molecular changes during physiological aging in mice
authors: Browder KC, Reddy P, Yamamoto M, Haghani A, Guillen IG, Sahu S, Wang C, Luque Y, Prieto J, Shi L, Shojima K, Hishida T, Lai Z, Li Q, Choudhury FK, Wong WR, Liang Y, Sangaraju D, Sandoval W, Esteban CR, Delicado EN, Garcia PG, Pawlak M, Vander Heiden JA, Horvath S, Jasper H, Izpisua Belmonte JC.
why: Studies longer-term partial reprogramming during normal aging in mice.
caution: Molecular/tissue improvements do not establish safe human systemic reprogramming.

title: Multi-omic rejuvenation of human cells by maturation phase transient reprogramming
authors: Gill D, Parry A, Santos F, Okkenhaug H, Todd CD, Hernando-Herraez I, Stubbs TM, Milagre I, Reik W.
why: Transient reprogramming shifts several aging-related measures in cultured fibroblasts.
caution: Human cells in a dish, not rejuvenated people; clock changes are surrogate outcomes.

title: Chemically induced reprogramming to reverse cellular aging
authors: Yang JH, Petty CA, Dixon-McDougall T, Lopez MV, Tyshkovskiy A, Maybury-Lewis S, Tian X, Ibrahim N, Chen Z, Griffin PT, Arnold M, Li J, Martinez OA, Behn A, Rogers-Hammond R, Angeli S, Gladyshev VN, Sinclair DA.
why: Screens chemical cocktails that shift cellular aging signatures.
caution: Cell assays do not prove human safety, durable rejuvenation or longer life.

title: Clearance of p16Ink4a-positive senescent cells delays ageing-associated disorders
authors: Baker DJ, Wijshake T, Tchkonia T, LeBrasseur NK, Childs BG, van de Sluis B, Kirkland JL, van Deursen JM.
why: Genetically clearing senescent cells delays selected disorders in progeroid mice.
caution: Engineered premature-aging mice; not a supplement trial.

title: Naturally occurring p16(Ink4a)-positive cells shorten healthy lifespan
authors: Baker DJ, Childs BG, Durik M, Wijers ME, Sieben CJ, Zhong J, Saltness RA, Jeganathan KB, Verzosa GC, Pezeshki A, Khazaie K, Miller JD, van Deursen JM.
why: Clearing p16-positive cells extends median lifespan in mouse cohorts.
caution: Genetic cell-clearance system, not direct evidence for a human drug regimen.

title: Senolytics improve physical function and increase lifespan in old age
authors: Xu M, Pirtskhalava T, Farr JN, Weigand BM, Palmer AK, Weivoda MM, Inman CL, Ogrodnik MB, Hachfeld CM, Fraser DG, Onken JL, Johnson KO, Verzosa GC, Langhi LGP, Weigl M, Giorgadze N, LeBrasseur NK, Miller JD, Jurk D, Singh RJ, Allison DB, Ejima K, Hubbard GB, Ikeno Y, Cubro H, Garovic VD, Hou X, Weroha SJ, Robbins PD, Niedernhofer LJ, Khosla S, Tchkonia T, Kirkland JL.
why: Senolytic treatment improves function and remaining survival in old mice.
caution: Includes human tissue experiments, but the lifespan evidence is in mice.

title: Fisetin is a senotherapeutic that extends health and lifespan
authors: Yousefzadeh MJ, Zhu Y, McGowan SJ, Angelini L, Fuhrmann-Stroissnigg H, Xu M, Ling YY, Melos KI, Pirtskhalava T, Inman CL, McGuckian C, Wade EA, Kato JI, Grassi D, Wentworth M, Burd CE, Arriaga EA, Ladiges WL, Tchkonia T, Kirkland JL, Robbins PD, Niedernhofer LJ.
why: Tests fisetin for senescence-related tissue and lifespan effects in mice.
caution: Human tissue work does not establish that taking fisetin extends human life.

title: Senolytics in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Results from a first-in-human, open-label, pilot study
authors: Justice JN, Nambiar AM, Tchkonia T, LeBrasseur NK, Pascual R, Hashmi SK, Prata L, Masternak MM, Kritchevsky SB, Musi N, Kirkland JL.
why: An open-label senolytic pilot tests feasibility in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
caution: 14 participants, no placebo control, adverse events; not healthy-person longevity evidence.

title: Senolytics decrease senescent cells in humans: Preliminary report from a clinical trial of Dasatinib plus Quercetin in individuals with diabetic kidney disease
authors: Hickson LJ, Langhi Prata LGP, Bobart SA, Evans TK, Giorgadze N, Hashmi SK, Herrmann SM, Jensen MD, Jia Q, Jordan KL, Kellogg TA, Khosla S, Koerber DM, Lagnado AB, Lawson DK, LeBrasseur NK, Lerman LO, McDonald KM, McKenzie TJ, Passos JF, Pignolo RJ, Pirtskhalava T, Saadiq IM, Schaefer KK, Textor SC, Victorelli SG, Volkman TL, Xue A, Wentworth MA, Wissler Gerdes EO, Zhu Y, Tchkonia T, Kirkland JL.
why: A small senolytic study measures changes in senescence markers in diabetic kidney disease.
caution: Nine participants, open label and short follow-up; biomarker change is not lifespan extension.

title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice
authors: Harrison DE, Strong R, Sharp ZD, Nelson JF, Astle CM, Flurkey K, Nadon NL, Wilkinson JE, Frenkel K, Carter CS, Pahor M, Javors MA, Fernandez E, Miller RA.
why: Late-life rapamycin extends survival in genetically heterogeneous mice.
caution: Mouse results do not establish a safe or effective human longevity regimen.

title: mTOR inhibition improves immune function in the elderly
authors: Mannick JB, Del Giudice G, Lattanzi M, Valiante NM, Praestgaard J, Huang B, Lonetto MA, Maecker HT, Kovarik J, Carson S, Glass DJ, Klickstein LB.
why: Tests an mTOR inhibitor against age-related vaccine-response impairment.
caution: Immune-response endpoint, not human lifespan or whole-body rejuvenation.

title: TORC1 inhibition enhances immune function and reduces infections in the elderly
authors: Mannick JB, Morris M, Hockey HP, Roma G, Beibel M, Kulmatycki K, Watkins M, Shavlakadze T, Zhou W, Quinn D, Glass DJ, Klickstein LB.
why: A phase 2a trial tests TORC1 inhibition, immune responses and infections in older adults.
caution: Read alongside the later phase 2b/3 report with a negative phase 3 primary endpoint.

title: Effect of long-term caloric restriction on DNA methylation measures of biological aging in healthy adults from the CALERIE trial
authors: Waziry R, Ryan CP, Corcoran DL, Huffman KM, Kobor MS, Kothari M, Graf GH, Kraus VB, Kraus WE, Lin DTS, Pieper CF, Ramaker ME, Bhapkar M, Das SK, Ferrucci L, Hastings WJ, Kebbe M, Parker DC, Racette SB, Shalev I, Schilling B, Belsky DW.
why: CALERIE analysis finds a small change in DunedinPACE after calorie restriction.
caution: Post hoc biomarker analysis; other age clocks did not significantly change; not mortality evidence.

title: Fasting-mimicking diet and markers/risk factors for aging, diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular disease
authors: Wei M, Brandhorst S, Shelehchi M, Mirzaei H, Cheng CW, Budniak J, Groshen S, Mack WJ, Guen E, Di Biase S, Cohen P, Morgan TE, Dorff T, Hong K, Michalsen A, Laviano A, Longo VD.
why: Tests cycles of a fasting-mimicking diet against metabolic and disease-risk markers.
caution: Short-term risk-marker changes, not proof of longer life or cancer prevention.

title: Nicotinamide riboside is uniquely and orally bioavailable in mice and humans
authors: Trammell SA, Schmidt MS, Weidemann BJ, Redpath P, Jaksch F, Dellinger RW, Li Z, Abel ED, Migaud ME, Brenner C.
why: Shows oral nicotinamide riboside can increase NAD-related metabolites.
caution: Bioavailability is not proof of anti-aging benefit.

title: Chronic nicotinamide riboside supplementation is well-tolerated and elevates NAD+ in healthy middle-aged and older adults
authors: Martens CR, Denman BA, Mazzo MR, Armstrong ML, Reisdorph N, McQueen MB, Chonchol M, Seals DR.
why: A short randomized crossover trial tests NR tolerability and NAD metabolism.
caution: Short-term target engagement; no demonstrated human lifespan extension.

title: Long-Term Administration of Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Mitigates Age-Associated Physiological Decline in Mice
authors: Mills KF, Yoshida S, Stein LR, Grozio A, Kubota S, Sasaki Y, Redpath P, Migaud ME, Apte RS, Uchida K, Yoshino J, Imai SI.
why: Long-term NMN treatment mitigates several age-related physiological changes in mice.
caution: Mouse physiology, not established human rejuvenation.

title: Nicotinamide mononucleotide increases muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic women
authors: Yoshino M, Yoshino J, Kayser BD, Patti GJ, Franczyk MP, Mills KF, Sindelar M, Pietka T, Patterson BW, Imai SI, Klein S.
why: Tests NMN against muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic postmenopausal women.
caution: A specific metabolic endpoint and population, not general age reversal.

title: DNA methylation age of human tissues and cell types
authors: Horvath S.
why: Introduces a multi-tissue DNA-methylation clock for age estimation.
caution: Prediction of age is not validation of a treatment or a direct measure of remaining life.

title: An epigenetic biomarker of aging for lifespan and healthspan
authors: Levine ME, Lu AT, Quach A, Chen BH, Assimes TL, Bandinelli S, Hou L, Baccarelli AA, Stewart JD, Li Y, Whitsel EA, Wilson JG, Reiner AP, Aviv A, Lohman K, Liu Y, Ferrucci L, Horvath S.
why: Develops PhenoAge using clinical-risk and DNA-methylation information.
caution: Predictive associations do not show that changing the clock improves survival.

title: DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan
authors: Lu AT, Quach A, Wilson JG, Reiner AP, Aviv A, Raj K, Hou L, Baccarelli AA, Li Y, Stewart JD, Whitsel EA, Assimes TL, Ferrucci L, Horvath S.
why: Develops GrimAge to predict mortality-related and healthspan-related outcomes.
caution: Risk prediction is not a causal test of rejuvenation.

title: DunedinPACE, a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging
authors: Belsky DW, Caspi A, Corcoran DL, Sugden K, Poulton R, Arseneault L, Baccarelli A, Chamarti K, Gao X, Hannon E, Harrington HL, Houts R, Kothari M, Kwon D, Mill J, Schwartz J, Vokonas P, Wang C, Williams BS, Moffitt TE.
why: Develops DunedinPACE as a blood-based estimate of the pace of aging.
caution: Useful research surrogate; changes need validation against clinical outcomes.

title: Reversal of epigenetic aging and immunosenescent trends in humans
authors: Fahy GM, Brooke RT, Watson JP, Good Z, Vasanawala SS, Maecker H, Leipold MD, Lin DTS, Kobor MS, Horvath S.
why: Reports immune and epigenetic-clock changes after a thymus-focused intervention.
caution: Small uncontrolled pilot; predicted lifespan is not observed lifespan extension.

title: Partial cellular reprogramming: A deep dive into an emerging rejuvenation technology
authors: Paine PT, Nguyen A, Ocampo A.
why: Reviews partial cellular reprogramming, translation challenges and commercial interest.
caution: A field overview, not evidence that systemic rejuvenation is ready for patients.

title: The hallmarks of aging
authors: López-Otín C, Blasco MA, Partridge L, Serrano M, Kroemer G.
why: The original nine-hallmark framework organizes mechanisms of mammalian aging.
caution: Read with the 2023 update; neither is a clinical treatment protocol.

title: Individual and additive effects of vitamin D, omega-3 and exercise on DNA methylation clocks of biological aging in older adults from the DO-HEALTH trial
authors: Bischoff-Ferrari HA, Gängler S, Wieczorek M, Belsky DW, Ryan J, Kressig RW, Stähelin HB, Theiler R, Dawson-Hughes B, Rizzoli R, Vellas B, Rouch L, Guyonnet S, Egli A, Orav EJ, Willett W, Horvath S.
why: DO-HEALTH analysis reports small methylation-clock changes with omega-3 and some combinations.
caution: Post hoc biomarker analysis, not demonstrated clinical age reversal or extra years of life.

title: Targeting the biology of ageing with mTOR inhibitors to improve immune function in older adults: phase 2b and phase 3 randomised trials
authors: Mannick JB, Teo G, Bernardo P, Quinn D, Russell K, Klickstein L, Marshall W, Shergill S.
why: Reports phase 2b and phase 3 RTB101 trials, including a negative phase 3 primary endpoint.
caution: Promising immune-gene signals did not translate into fewer clinically symptomatic respiratory illnesses in phase 3.
